title: Manage scheduled Annals source imports
summary: Queue, prioritize, dispatch, pause, inspect, interrupt, or recover bounded sets of source imports handled through the Annals inbox.
use_when: The configured filesystem inbox, its one-attempt job envelopes, dispatch controls, or bounded retry events must be observed or operated.
A scheduled delivery failure must be diagnosed across Annals domain state and its correlated Nucleus job.
do_not_use_when: One explicitly selected source should be integrated manually.
The proposed recovery edits receipts or archive directories directly.
The desired retry window is omitted, open-ended, or based on future failures.
outcome: A durable and inspectable inbox state transition or report that preserves immutable attempts, archive history, explicit priority, and bounded retry provenance.
effects: Registration moves settled incoming files into durable queued envelopes; direct enqueue copies explicit files and leaves originals unchanged.
Dispatch starts source deliveries and may invoke Nucleus, apply corpus reconciliations, and consume Codex allowance.
The storage gate defers an ordinary claim until the configured reserve is available on both Annals filesystems; direct enqueue rejects a copy that would cross the spool reserve.
Pause blocks new dispatch but permits registration; interruption archives one exact processing job as failed or skipped.
A retry event preserves originals and creates fresh linked child jobs for one frozen inclusive failed-delivery interval.
authority: Annals owns spool envelopes, queue order, priority lanes, source-delivery records, retry events, reconciliation application, and recovery policy.
Nucleus owns only each liaison attempt and its raw runtime records; Nucleus never chooses an Annals retry.
success: Status or event reports identify queue, active job, pause, maintenance, archive, and outcome state without relying on process inspection.
A storage-gated ordinary job remains queued with attempts zero and resumes automatically on a later activation once the condition clears.
A run or retry report, not process exit alone, accounts for every attempted item and durable result.
Original failed jobs and deliveries remain unchanged after retry.
failure_and_recovery: Product-owned schema-two schedule definitions select halt-until-approved. The first abnormal attempt ends the current run. Clockwork permits later activations before the shared service-health threshold. By default, five consecutive failed read-only checks, at least 60 seconds apart, establish the halt and alert eligibility together. Healthy or inactive checks, including operator pause, clear a pending failure episode. Established halts require exact binding resume approval; definition switches, deployment and product resume/retry preserve them. Product domain state and explicit retries remain product-owned.
Every inbox job has at most one processing attempt; never move a terminal envelope back to queued.
A storage probe failure prevents a claim and exits nonzero; insufficient storage halts an attended retry until the operator continues it.
When low storage closes the gate, preserve the queued work and leave storage remediation or a reserve change to the user under explicit target-scoped consent.
Unexpected model or runtime failure archives the current job and halts the activation or retry event; continue only through the supported command.
Pause before interruption when the next ordinary job must remain queued, and require paused quiescence before starting or continuing a retry event.
privacy: Inbox envelopes retain unchanged source material and receipts; Annals and Nucleus operational state may retain complete source and model context.
Spool, database, logs, and retry archives belong to the user's private application boundary.
does_not_authorize: Editing spool receipts or moving archived envelopes manually.

Deleting, truncating, pruning, moving, compressing, or otherwise clearing user data as storage remediation, or lowering or disabling the storage reserve, without the user's explicit consent for the exact target and scope.
An unbounded retry or a second attempt for the same job.
Restarting Nucleus while an Annals attempt is active.

consumers.statement: Local operators use this procedure to inspect, admit, prioritize, dispatch, pause, interrupt, or recover one configured Annals inbox.

preconditions.statement: Select and verify one prepared library, immutable kind, expected identity, config, and spool. Dispatch also requires the inbox feature's storage, authentication, and prompt prerequisites. Retry requires paused quiescence and exact eligible bounds.

inputs.statement: The supported commands take explicit files, exact job/event IDs, priority lane, disposition, and bounded failed-delivery anchors with optional operator reason.
Receipt edits, terminal-envelope requeue, retry-all, open bounds, future-failure selection, and a second attempt per job are unsupported.

outputs.statement: Status, run, preview, and event receipts preserve all queue, gate, attempt, domain, and halt facts defined by the required inbox feature. Add --details for the full event mapping; increase positive --limit for event pages beyond the default 20.

data_semantics.statement: The required inbox feature owns complete queue, receipt, delivery, retry, failure-policy, and recovery semantics. A procedure verifies product records and does not infer domain success from process state or exit code alone.

identity_and_units.statement: Choose exact job and event IDs and inclusive anchors in failed-delivery completion order. Each job remains a one-attempt identity, and retries create linked children rather than changing originals.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Inspect status before controls or recovery and verify returned durable outcomes afterward. Retry preview does not freeze membership; start freezes the complete eligible interval.
No drain deadline, schedule interval, completion latency, or storage-restoration service level is promised.

access.statement: Read-only procedures need prepared readable state and applicable locks; mutations require authority for their specific effects. Registered names and explicit operator config select the same supported boundary.
Direct spool/SQLite editing and host-wide storage or service control are unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Pause before interruption to preserve successors. Start/continue only while paused and quiescent, and continue only unattempted children. Verify durable item outcomes before resuming ordinary dispatch.

After a scheduled abend, inspect and recover the Annals domain result separately; resume the exact Clockwork incident only after explicit approval. Product resume, retry, deployment, and dependency recovery do not clear it.

operational_limits.statement: The operation preserves one attempt per job, frozen bounded membership, distinct controls, and existing domain success. Low storage is a stop only; exact target-scoped user consent is required before cleanup or reserve change.
No queue capacity, source-size, fairness, throughput, or wall-clock completion bound is promised here.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Operation contract six retains its identity and supported routes. Required inbox feature two owns detail; provider release, library schema, receipt shape, and dependent protocols remain independent.
No additional spool-format support window or deprecation period is promised.

reliances.statement: This procedure requires the Annals inbox feature for all supported state, effects, controls, accounting, and recovery promises.

steps: Select and verify the prepared library, expected immutable identity, admission kind, config, and spool; read inbox status before changing controls.
Use general-library register or enqueue only for admitted source files; use the producer inlet for a decisions library.
Choose explicit priority or dispatch effects. Dispatch can examine new work and apply a reconciliation immediately; verify the durable run report.
Pause before interrupting an exact active job when successors must remain queued. Verify the requested terminal disposition.
Preview an exact bounded failed-delivery interval. Start only after paused quiescence and complete eligibility, then read the retained event report.
Correct actionable halts and continue only unattempted children. Verify completed membership and item outcomes before resuming ordinary dispatch.
Inspect a scheduled failure incident and recover the Annals domain result separately. Resume the exact Clockwork binding only after explicit approval for that incident.
checkpoints: Library identity, kind, spool, controls, and required prepared read state are verified before operation.
Each claimed job has at most one attempt, and a retry preserves every original and freezes exact membership.
The durable Annals result is checked even when Nucleus runtime or process exit later fails.
Resume clears only the intended operator pause; Clockwork incidents and deployment maintenance remain separate.
Low storage preserves queued input and no cleanup or reserve change occurs without exact target-scoped user consent.
adaptation: Scope commands by registered name or the explicit operator config for the selected library.
Use the decisions binding and producer-only admission route when the immutable library kind is decisions.
Use event details for complete original-to-child verification and positive page limits when the default selection is insufficient.
stop_when: The selected identity, role, locks, prepared state, or recovery material cannot be verified.
A storage probe, authentication, unexpected model/runtime failure, or operator interruption halts attended work.
A retry interval contains an ineligible or missing original or changed archived material.
Recovery requires direct receipt/SQLite edits, a second attempt for one job, unbounded retry, or storage remediation without exact user consent.
Clockwork continuation lacks explicit approval for the retained incident.
